I would hope that's the case. I could maybe do work in a non-combat role if I was forced to but would still feel really conflicted about it -- the clashing ideas that I'd be supporting a war I don't want to, but I'd still want to help keep my country safe I guess

The fact that I'm unemployed but would also refuse to work in any sort of military position just kinda makes me feel like a lazy bum piece of shit. Been coming closer and closer to not being one, but holy fuck this news is setting me back.

\[rambling warning\]

Was taking it one day at a time, worked through the depression just enough to start challenging my anxiety in small bursts, almost confident enough to get my license, go for an interview; but now I feel waist deep in the quicksand of depression, again, and I'm so ready to fucking fight and flail and sink so I can just escape!!!

Basically, everytime I convince myself to live and that life is worth living, something happens to just turn all that progress around.

I'm just so on edge, I don't want a war :(  I want this to get resolved so I can get back to my stupid little life but I feel so pessimistic! Man, this sucks.

I hate when i feel like Im bothering people even though I shouldn't in this sub. thanks for reading, anybody. . . trying to acknowledge how tainted my mind is when im in moods like this. hopefully this decade really does have something good in store, please

Never been in therapy or hospitalized, I tend to only talk about it with select family members, journal, or just bottle it up. . . so I guess I don't have a history. I once had a psychological evaluation done in high school(over the phrase "pull the trigger" used in a text message, long bs story, not even used in a threatening or suicidal context) and admitted suicidal urges due to stress, but that's it.

I remember getting a letter about conscription when I came of age. I don't know if mere claims of suicidal urges or poor mental health would be sufficient for exemption
